2016_101_111516mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of November 15, 2016 pairs a routine consent agenda — October minutes, a $93,013.20 copy paper award to Midland Paper, a stormwater management resolution, and the September 2016 Treasurer's Report showing $9,696,782.68 in total disbursements — with two action items. The consequential one is a bond parameters resolution authorizing the "2017 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation)" in an amount not to exceed $40,000,000, the second series drawn on the $125,000,000 authorization approved by Troy voters November 5, 2013. The other approves Trustee Gary Hauff's attendance at the NSBA Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C.

**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, 7:00 p.m., November 15, 2016, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000); cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools. Item 2.A recognizes Troy High School wrestling coach Don Hill, introduced by Principal Remo Roncone.

**Consent agenda (items A–F).** Minutes of the October 4, 2016 workshop (6:00–10:06 p.m.; policy sections C, D and E), the October 18, 2016 special workshop (5:45–8:52 p.m.; Yeo & Yeo audit report) and the October 18, 2016 regular meeting; copy paper; stormwater management approval; and the September 2016 Treasurer's Report. The October 18 minutes record Resolutions 16-079 through 16-086, each 7-0: recognition of 62 National Merit semifinalists; the hire of James Helfrich; the 2016-2017 Sex Education Advisory Board; acceptance of the audited 2016 financial statements presented by Yeo & Yeo partner David Youngstrom; a $33,200.00 award to Riegle Timing Consultants LLC for aquatic sports timing from the 2016-2017 Activities Fund; and withdrawal from the Adair lawsuit effective October 18, 2016, rescinding the Board's action of May 12, 1998.

**Copy paper, Bid 9828.** Purchasing Supervisor Todd Hensley reported six responses from seven invited bidders on 4,200 cases and recommended Midland Paper, Inc.

| Bidder | Per case | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Midland Paper (award) | $22.15 | $93,013.20 |
| Veritiv Operating Company | $22.27 | $93,534.00 |
| Contract Paper Group | $22.68 | $95,256.00 |
| Costco Wholesale | $22.87 | $96,054.00 |
| School Specialty | $24.42 | $102,564.00 |
| Audio Visual Equipment & Supplies | $26.99 | $113,358.00 |

**Stormwater.** The resolution commits the district to its NPDES municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) permit under the Michigan DEQ Water Bureau — prohibiting illicit discharges and connections, obtaining Part 91 permits for projects disturbing one or more acres, complying with Rule 323.2190. Arch Environmental Group (project AE160001; October 25, 2016 letter from Jenna Gillmore Sendra to Director of Operations Rob Carson) explains it stands in place of an ordinance and removes 2012 Administrative Consent Order language.

**Treasurer's Report, September 2016** (Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services):

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Total check disbursements | $7,541,740.59 |
| ACH debits | $12,638.34 |
| Outgoing wire transfers | $1,966,300.24 |
| P-Card purchases | $197,349.65 |
| Prior period void disbursements | ($21,246.14) |
| Total disbursements in period | $9,696,782.68 |

General Fund (101, 120, 122) revenue budget $143,026,065 against $19,737,120 actual; expenditure budget $142,948,405 against $18,766,607 actual and $72,925,586 encumbered; fund balance $19,659,870 at September 1 and $19,737,530 at September 30. Closing September balances elsewhere: debt service funds $3,495,991, consolidated capital projects $41,536,791, food service $1,320,870, adult and community education $633,846, facilities rental $522,113, Troy Career Center $0.

**Item 8.A — Series 2 bonds.** The resolution authorizes the "2017 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation)," not to exceed $40,000,000, as the second series under the $125,000,000 authorization approved November 5, 2013; the first series, $52,710,000, was issued January 29, 2014. Final maturity no later than sixteen years, true interest cost not exceeding 5.00%, negotiated sale with Stifel, Nicolaus & Company as senior managing underwriter or placement agent, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone as bond counsel, Public Financial Management as financial advisor. PFM's presale package prices $39,420,000 dated 2/1/17 at a 2.42364% true interest cost with gross production of $40,155,847.35, and holds the debt levy at 4.700 mills for both the 2016 and 2017 levies, a net increase of 0.000.

**Item 10.A.** Under Board Policy B-2001, Workshops and Conferences, approval of Trustee Gary Hauff's attendance at the NSBA Advocacy Institute, Marriott Marquis, Washington, D.C., January 29–31, 2017; registration $695, rooms $244 plus tax.

Packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, November 15, 2016, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us), cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Item 2.A, the TSD Mission Moment, honors Don Hill, wrestling coach at Troy High School, introduced by Principal Remo Roncone. The consent agenda groups six items: minutes of the October 4, 2016 workshop, the October 18, 2016 special workshop and the October 18, 2016 regular meeting; copy paper; stormwater management approval; and the Treasurer's Report for September 2016.

**October minutes.** The October 4 workshop at the Administration Building ran 6:00 p.m. to 10:06 p.m. under President Philippart, with Trustees Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood, Superintendent Machesky, administrators Dziatczak, Griffor and Harris, and Kevin Sutton of Lusk Albertson; it covered policy sections C, D and E, staff evaluation, early childhood, testing results and an AP report. The October 18 special workshop at the Services Building ran 5:45 p.m. to 8:52 p.m. for the Yeo & Yeo audit report. The October 18 regular meeting, opened at 7:00 p.m. with four student representatives, roughly 25 audience members and Yeo & Yeo audit partner David Youngstrom, adopted eight resolutions, all 7-0: 16-079 recognizing 62 National Merit Scholarship semifinalists (more than one million students from some 22,000 high schools entered; 16,000 seniors selected; the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT), read by Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak; 16-080 approving the September 6 and September 20 minutes and the August 2016 Treasurer's Report; 16-081 hiring James Helfrich; 16-082 seating the 2016-2017 Sex Education Advisory Board under co-chairs Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins; 16-083 accepting the audited 2016 financial statements after Youngstrom's review of fund balance history and future challenges including retirement rate increases, special education costs and the unfunded pension liability; 16-084 awarding aquatic sports timing equipment and installation to Riegle Timing Consultants LLC for $33,200.00 from the 2016-2017 Activities Fund; 16-085 rescinding the Board's May 12, 1998 action and withdrawing as a participant in the Adair lawsuit effective October 18, 2016; and 16-086 adopting Board committee assignments. Also recorded: Morse Elementary's "Morse Summer Nights" presented by Principal Stephanie Zendler; Special Education Director Kathy Jagels named 2016 Gregory Gwisdalla Special Education Administrator of the Year by the Special Education Administrators of Oakland County on September 9; a 2015-2016 evaluation summary by Assistant Superintendent Jordan Harris; and the departure of Ms. Underwood and Mrs. Edmunds from the Board at the end of December. Adjournment 8:41 p.m.; minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**Copy paper, Bid 9828 (2016-17 school year).** Memorandum of October 18, 2016 from Purchasing Supervisor Todd Hensley (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48093; 248 823-4091) to Assistant Superintendent Rick West: invitations went to seven potential bidders and six responded on a case quantity of 4,200. Award recommended to Midland Paper, Inc. at $22.15 per case, $93,013.20. Other bids: Veritiv Operating Company $22.27 / $93,534.00; Contract Paper Group, Inc. $22.68 / $95,256.00; Costco Wholesale $22.87 / $96,054.00; School Specialty, Inc. $24.42 / $102,564.00; Audio Visual Equipment & Supplies $26.99 / $113,358.00.

**Stormwater management.** District facilities lie within the "Detroit" urbanized area and discharge through a municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4) regulated by the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality – Water Bureau under an NPDES permit. The resolution adopts the district's Stormwater Management Program Plan, prohibits illicit discharges and illicit connections including connections made in the past, addresses post-construction runoff for disturbances exceeding 1 acre, commits to a Part 91 permit for projects disturbing one or more acres and to Rule 323.2190, and instructs the Superintendent to enforce it. An October 25, 2016 letter from Jenna Gillmore Sendra of Arch Environmental Group, Inc. (project AE160001) to Director of Operations Rob Carson, 1140 Rankin Drive, Troy, Michigan 48083, ties it to the 2012 Administrative Consent Order that followed the district's removal from the Nesting Agreement with the City of Troy and the new application required in April 2015; the resolution is used in place of an ordinance.

**Item 8.A — Series 2 bonds.** The cover sheet states the $125,000,000 bond issue was passed by voters November 5, 2013, that the district wishes to issue a second series not to exceed $40,000,000, and names Dr. Richard Machesky and Rick West as authorized to accept a purchase offer; the attached resolution and exhibits instead designate the issue the "2017 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation)" and define the Authorized Officer as the Superintendent. The resolution recites the January 29, 2014 issuance of $52,710,000 of 2014 School Building and Site Bonds as the first series, pledges unlimited tax levies under Section 6 and Section 16 of Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, and sets terms: $5,000 denominations, May 1 or November 1 maturities, final maturity not later than sixteen years, negotiated sale at a true interest cost not exceeding 5.00%, semi-annual interest, book-entry through The Depository Trust Company, a levy commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2017, and continuing disclosure under SEC Rule 15c2-12. It appoints Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated as senior managing underwriter or placement agent, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. as bond counsel and Public Financial Management, Inc. as financial advisor, and seeks qualification under Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001 and Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005; the Open Meetings Act certification is signed by Secretary Paula Fleming. Exhibit A requires annual EMMA filings within six months of fiscal year end commencing with the year ended June 30, 2016, updating eleven tables (property valuations, tax rates, state aid payments, tax levies and collections, pension fund, debt statement, legal debt margin, school enrollment and general fund budget summary among them), plus fourteen material events reportable within ten business days.

PFM's October 21, 2016 letter to James M. Crowley of Miller, Canfield (150 West Jefferson, Suite 2500, Detroit, Michigan 48226), signed by Managing Director Paul R. Stauder, anticipates a mid-December private placement and sets delegation parameters of purchase price not less than 100%, TIC not to exceed 5%, placement agent fee not more than $7,000 and bond term not more than 16 years; the bonds will not be bank qualified but will be qualified for SLRF participation. Estimated sources and uses for $39,420,000 show par of $39,420,000.00 plus production of $735,847.35 for total sources of $40,155,847.35, applied to a capital projects account of $39,844,079.03, underwriter's discount of $157,680.00 at 0.400%, and costs of issuance of $154,088.32 (bond attorney $52,905.85, PFM $47,982.47, Moody's $36,000.00, paying agent $500.00, security report filing $1,000.00, official statement $3,500.00, state qualification $11,800.00, Municipal Advisory Council $400.00). The production report, dated and delivered 2/1/17 with first coupon 11/1/17 and first call 5/1/26 at 100.00%, runs serials from $3,770,000 due 5/1/18 to $4,825,000 due 5/1/32 at coupons of 2.000% to 3.000%, with gross production $40,155,847.35 (101.86669%), bid $39,998,167.35, bond years 397,800.00, average coupon 2.60569%, average life 10.091, net interest cost $9,787,285.78, true interest cost 2.42364% and arbitrage yield 2.26530%. The estimated millage schedule holds the 2016 and 2017 levies at 4.700 mills for a net increase of 0.000, shows 2016 taxable value of $3,630,712,070 (up 0.75% over 2015's $3,603,511,590) with a five-year historical average of 0.57% and a twenty-year average of 1.41%, existing unlimited-tax debt of $111,925,000, exempt personal property of $35,159,995, and column totals of $229,156,302 in total existing and proposed debt and $227,703,361 net. The running tally of unissued bond amounts lists Series 2014 at $52,710,000, Series 2017 at $39,420,000 and Series 2020 at $27,000,000. Existing debt schedules cover the 2013 School Building and Site Bonds ($11,900,000, NIC 2.000%), 2014 School Bus Bonds ($3,100,000, NIC 1.930%) and 2015 Refunding Bonds ($14,260,000, NIC 2.923%), with combined totals of $59,370,000 principal and $71,113,558 principal and interest.

**Item 10.A — NSBA Advocacy Institute.** Citing Board Policy B-2001, Workshops and Conferences, which requires prior approval by resolution for out-of-state meetings, the Board considers approving Trustee Gary Hauff's attendance at the National School Boards Association Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C., January 29–31, 2017. Attached NSBA printouts dated 11/15/2016 give the venue as the Marriott Marquis, 901 Massachusetts Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20001, a registration fee of $695, room rates of $244 plus a 14% tax, a reservation cut-off of January 9, 2017 through Convention Management Resources, and presidential historian Doris Kearns Goodwin as featured speaker; NSBA's events-search page instead lists the Advocacy Institute as January 28–31, 2017, and gives NSBA's address as 1680 Duke St. FL2, Alexandria, VA 22314-3493.
